#Text= as Saint Mary  '  s Falls, or the _Sault_,[27] as it is more generally and
#Text= appropriately called.
#Text=This fish resorts here in vast numbers, and is in
#Text= season after the autumnal equinox, and continues so till the ice begins
#Text= to run.
#Text=It is worthy the attention of ichthyologists.
#Text=It is a
#Text= remarkable, but not singular fact in its natural history, that it is
#Text= perpetually found in the attitude of ascent at these falls.
#Text=It is taken
#Text= only in the swift water at the foot of the last leap or descent.
#Text=Into
#Text= this swift water the Indians push their canoes.
#Text=It requires great skill
#Text= and dexterity for this.
#Text=The fishing canoe is of small size.
#Text=It is
#Text= steered by a man in the stern.
#Text=The fisherman takes his stand in the
#Text= bows, sometimes bestriding the light and frail vessel from gunwale to
#Text= gunwale, having a scoop-net in his hands.
#Text=This net has a long slender
#Text= handle, ten feet or more in length.
#Text=The net is made of strong twine,
#Text= open at the top, like an entomologist  '  s.
#Text=When the canoe has been run
#Text= into the uppermost rapids, and a school of fish is seen below or
#Text= alongside, he dexterously puts down his net, and having swooped up a
#Text= number of the fish, instantly reverses it in water, whips it up, and
#Text= discharges its contents into the canoe.
#Text=This he repeats till his canoe
#Text= is loaded, when he shoots out of the tail of the rapids, and makes for
#Text=shore.
#Text=The fish will average three pounds, but individuals are sometimes
#Text= two and three times that weight.
#Text=It is shad-shaped, with well-developed
#Text= scales, easily removed, but has the mouth of the sucker, very small.
#Text=The
#Text= flesh is perfectly white and firm, with very few bones.
#Text=It is boiled by
#Text= the Indians in pure water, in a peculiar manner, the kettle hung high
#Text= above a small blaze; and thus cooked, it is eaten with the liquid for a
#Text= gravy, and is delicate and delicious.
#Text=If boiled in the ordinary way, by
#Text= a low hung pot and quick fire, it is soft and comparatively flabby.
#Text=It
#Text= is also broiled by the inhabitants, on a gridiron, after cutting it open
#Text= on the back, and brought on the table slightly browned.
#Text=This must be
#Text= done, like a steak, quickly.
#Text=It is the most delicious when immediately
#Text= taken from the water, and connoisseurs will tell you, by its taste at
#Text= the table, whether it is immediately from the water, or has lain any
#Text= time before cooking.
#Text=It is sometimes made into small ovate masses,
#Text= dipped into batter, and fried in butter, and in this shape, it is called
#Text= _petite pâte._ It is also chowdered or baked in a pie.
#Text=It is the great
#Text= resource of the Indians and the French, and of the poor generally at
#Text= these falls, who eat it with potatoes, which are abundantly raised here.
#Text=It is also a standing dish with all.

#Text=_Man-kind_ and _bird-kind_ have concurred in

#Text=We have witnessed the long-drawn flight of swans,

#Text=Singing birds have long since

#Text=Ducks, all but a very few, have also silently disappeared, and
#Text= have probably gone to pick up spicy roots in the Susquehannah
#Text= or Altamaha.
#Text=Prescient in the changes of the season, they have been the first to go.
#Text=Men, who can endure greater changes and vicissitudes than all the animal
#Text= creation put together, have lingered longer; but at last one after
#Text= another has left Pa-wa-teeg, till all who _can_ go have gone.

#Text=_January 1st_.
#Text=This is a day of hilarity here, as in New York.
#Text=Gayety
#Text= and good humor appear on every countenance.
#Text=Visiting from house to house
#Text= is the order.
#Text=The humblest individual is expected to make his appearance
#Text= in the routine, and "has his claims allowed."
#Text=The French custom of
#Text= salutation prevails.
#Text=The Indians are not the last to remember the day.
#Text=To them, it is a season of privileges, although, alas!
#Text=it is only the

#Text=Standing in an official relation to them, I was

#Text=_28th_.
#Text=It is a year ago to-day since I visited the tomb of Washington,
#Text= at Mount Vernon.
#Text=There were three representatives in Congress, in
#Text= company.
#Text=We left the city of Washington in the morning, in a private
#Text= carriage, and drove down in good season.
#Text=I looked about the tomb
#Text= narrowly for some memento to bring away, and found some mineralogical
#Text= fragments on the small mound over the tomb, which would bear the
#Text=application of their book names.
#Text=On coming back through Alexandria, we
#Text= dined at a public hotel, where, among other productions of the season,
#Text= we had cucumbers.
#Text=What a contrast in climate to my present position!
#Text=Here, as the eyes search the fields, heaps of snow are still seen in
#Text= shaded situations, and the ice still disfigures the bays and
#Text= indentations of the shore in some places, as if it were animated with a
#Text= determination to hold out against the power of the sun to the utmost.
#Text=Nature, however, indicates its great vernal throe.
#Text=White fish were first
#Text= taken during the season, this day, which is rare
#Text=.

#Text=Dr.
#Text=Martyn Paine, of New York, proposes a system of

#Text=The large and fine collection of mineralogical
#Text= and geological specimens which I brought from Missouri and other parts
#Text= of the Mississippi valley in 1819, appears to have had an effect on the
#Text= prevalent taste for these subjects, and at least, it has fixed the eyes
#Text= of naturalists on my position on the frontiers.
#Text=Cabinets of minerals
#Text= have been in vogue for about nine or ten years.
#Text=Mr.
#Text=Maclure, of
#Text= Philadelphia, Colonel Gibbs, of New Haven, and Drs.
#Text=De Witt, Bruce and
#Text= Mitchill, of New York, and above Profs.
#Text=Silliman and Cleveland, may be
#Text=said to have originated the taste.
#Text=Before their day, minerals were
#Text= regarded as mere "stones."
#Text=Now, it is rare to find a college or academy
#Text= without, at least, the nucleus of a cabinet.
#Text=By transferring my
#Text= collection here, I have increased very much my own means of intellectual
#Text= enjoyment and resistance to the power of solitariness, if it has not
#Text= been the means of promoting discovery in others
#Text=.

#Text= _4th.
#Text=Fatalism_,--An Indian, called Wabishkipenace, _The White Bird_,
#Text= brings an express mail from the sub-agency of La Pointe, in Lake
#Text= Superior.
#Text=This proved to be the individual who, in 1820, acted as one of
#Text= the guides of the exploring expedition to the Copper Rock, on the
#Text= Ontonagon River.
#Text=Trifles light as air arouse an Indian  '  s suspicions, and
#Text= the circumstance of his being thus employed by the government agents,
#Text= was made use of by his fellows to his prejudice.
#Text=They told him that this
#Text= act was displeasing to the Great Spirit, who had visited him with his
#Text= displeasure.
#Text=Whatever influence this idea had on others, on
#Text= Wabishkipenace it seemed to tell.
#Text=He looked the image of despair.
#Text=He
#Text= wore his hair long, and was nearly naked.
#Text=He had a countenance of the
#Text=most melancholy cast.
#Text=Poverty itself could not be poorer.
#Text=Now, he
#Text= appears to have taken courage, and is willing once more to enter into
#Text= the conflicts of life.
#Text=But, alas!
#Text=what are these conflicts with an
#Text= Indian?
#Text=A mere struggle for meat and bread enough to live
#Text=.
#Text=_13th_.
#Text=This is a day long to be remembered in my domestic annals, as it
#Text= carried to the tomb the gem of a once happy circle, the cherished
#Text= darling of it, in the person of a beloved, beautiful, intellectually
#Text= promising, and only son.
#Text=William Henry had not yet quite completed his
#Text= third year, and yet such had been the impression created by his manly
#Text= precocity, his decision of character, perpetual liveliness of temper and
#Text= manners, and sweet and classic lineaments, and attachable traits, that
#Text= he appeared to have lived a long time.
#Text=The word _time_ is, indeed, a
#Text= relative term, and ever means much or little, as much or little has been
#Text= enjoyed or suffered.
#Text=Our enjoyment of him, and communion with him, was
#Text= intimate.
#Text=From the earliest day of his existence, his intelligence and
#Text= quick expressive eye was remarkable, and all his waking hours were full
#Text= of pleasing innocent action and affectionate appreciation.
#Text=We took him to the city of New York during the winter of 1824-25, where
#Text=he made many friends and had many admirers.
#Text=He was always remembered by
#Text= the youthful name of Willy and _Penaci_, or the bird--a term that was
#Text= playfully bestowed by the Chippewas while he was still in his cradle.
#Text=He
#Text= was, indeed, a bird in our circle, for the agility of his motions, the
#Text= liveliness of his voice, and the diamond sparkle of his full hazel eyes,
#Text= reminded one of nothing so much.
#Text=The month of March was more than
#Text= usually changeable in its temperature, with disagreeable rains and much
#Text= humidity, which nearly carried away the heavy amount of snow on the
#Text= ground.
#Text=A cold and croup rapidly developed themselves, and no efforts of
#Text= skill or kindness had power to arrest its fatal progress.
#Text=He sank under
#Text= it about eleven o  '  clock at night.
#Text=Such was the rapidity of this fatal
#Text= disease, that his silver playful voice still seemed to ring through the
#Text= house when he lay a placid corpse.
#Text=Several poetic tributes to his memory
#Text= were made, but none more touching than some lines from his own mother,
#Text= which are fit to be preserved as a specimen of native composition.[47]
#Text=
#Text= [Footnote 47:
#Text= Who was it nestled on my breast,
#Text= And on my cheek sweet kisses prest,
#Text= And in whose smile I felt so blest?
#Text=Sweet Willy.
#Text=Who hail  '  d my form as home I stept,
#Text= And in my arms so eager leapt,
#Text= And to my bosom joyous crept?
#Text=My Willy.
#Text=Who was it wiped my tearful eye,
#Text= And kiss  '  d away the coming sigh,
#Text= And smiling, bid me say, "good boy?"
#Text=Sweet Willy.
#Text=Who was it, looked divinely fair,
#Text= Whilst lisping sweet the evening pray  '  r,
#Text= Guileless and free from earthly care?
#Text=My Willy.
#Text=Where is that voice attuned to love,
#Text= That bid me say "my darling dove?"
#Text=But, oh!
#Text=that soul has flown above,
#Text=Sweet Willy.
#Text=Whither has fled the rose  '  s hue?
#Text=The lily  '  s whiteness blending grew
#Text= Upon thy cheek--so fair to view,
#Text= My Willy.
#Text=Oft have I gaz  '  d with rapt delight,
#Text= Upon those eyes that sparkled bright,
#Text= Emitting beams of joy and light!
#Text=Sweet Willy.
#Text=Oft have I kiss  '  d that forehead high,
#Text= Like polished marble to the eye,
#Text= And blessing, breathed an anxious sigh,
#Text= For Willy.
#Text=My son!
#Text=thy coral lips are pale--
#Text= Can I believe the heart-sick tale,
#Text= That I thy loss must ever wail?
#Text=My Willy.
#Text=The clouds in darkness seemed to low  '  r,
#Text= The storm has past with awful pow  '  r,
#Text= And nipt my tender, beauteous flow  '  r!
#Text=Sweet Willy.
#Text=But soon my spirit will be free,
#Text= And I my lovely son shall see,
#Text= For God, I know did this decree!
#Text=My Willy.
#Text= ]

#Text= _17th_.
#Text=This being St.
#Text=Patrick  '  s day, we dined with our excellent,
#Text= warm-hearted, and truly sympathizing friend, Mr.
#Text=Johnston, in a private
#Text= way.
#Text=He is the soul of hospitality, honor, friendship, and love, and no
#Text= one can be in his company an hour without loving and admiring a man who
#Text= gave up everything at home to raise up a family of most interesting
#Text= children in the heart of the American wilderness.
#Text=No man  '  s motives have
#Text= been more mistaken, no one has been more wronged, in public and private,
#Text=fuel, books, and studies.
#Text=Besides the fruitful theme of the Indian
#Text= language, I amused myself, in the early part of the season, by writing a
#Text= review for one of the periodicals, and with keeping up, throughout the
#Text= season, an extensive correspondence with friends and men of letters in
#Text= various parts of the Union.
#Text=I revised and refreshed myself in some of my
#Text= early studies, I continued to read whatever I could lay my hands on
#Text= respecting the philosophy of language.
#Text=Appearances of spring--the more
#Text= deepened sound of the falls, the floating of large cakes of ice from the
#Text= great northern depository, Lake Superior, and the return of some early
#Text= species of ducks and other birds--presented themselves as harbingers of
#Text= spring almost unawares.
#Text=It is still wintry cold during the nights and
#Text= mornings, but there is a degree of solar heat at noon which betokens the
#Text= speedy decline of the reign of frosts and snows.
#Text=The Indians, to whom the rising of the sap in its capillary vessels in
#Text= the rock-maple is the sign of a sort of carnival, are now in the midst
#Text= of their season of sugar-making.
#Text=It is one of their old customs to move,
#Text= men, women, children, and dogs, to their accustomed sugar-forests about
#Text= the 20th of March.

#Text=I could not hesitate as to the course which duty
#Text= proscribed to me, under these important circumstances, and determined to
#Text= proceed to Washington, although the Secretary and acting Governor of the
#Text= Territory, Mr.
#Text=Horner, on being consulted by letter, refused his assent
#Text= to this step.
#Text=His want of proper information on the subject, being but
#Text= recently come to the territory, did not appear to be such as to justify
#Text= me in remaining on the island, while the question had been carried by
#Text= the Indians themselves to, and was, probably, to be decided at
#Text= Washington before another season.
#Text=I determined, therefore, to proceed to
#Text= Washington, taking one of the latest vessels for the season, on their
#Text= return from the ports on Lake Michigan.
